newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. grain exports normal despite mishap - Zen-Noh.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grain exports normal despite mishap - Zen-Noh.

text.p: Japanese agricultural cooperative Zen-Noh said on Tuesday that its U.S. grain shipments to Japan were proceeding as normal despite an accident at a unit's loading elevator in Louisiana last week.

The accident occurred last Thursday when a vessel loading 50,000 tonnes of corn destined for Saudi Arabia "made contact with the dock and a structure at the Zen-Noh Grain Corp terminal," a Zen-Noh Grain Corp official said last week.
The grain loading facility is located in Convent, Louisiana, and has an annual handling capacity of 400 million to 500 million bushels, he said.
Taiwanese grain traders said freight costs from the Pacific Northwest may rise if damage to the U.S. unit's loading elevator caused delays along the Mississippi River.
Zen-Noh Grain Corp is a U.S.-based subsidiary of the National Federation of Agricultural Co-operative Associations (Zen-Noh), Japan's largest grain importer.
"We're going to receive a detailed damage assessment from engineers today or tomorrow, but we can't tell when its loading operations can resume at this stage," an official of Zen-Noh in Tokyo said.
Zen-Noh Grain Corp has asked other U.S. grain firms for help in loading grain destined for Japan, he said. -- Tokyo Commodities desk (+81-3-3432-7391)
